findings.before: The Bavarian Palace Department credits Cuvilliés with the design, while Wikipedia credits the hall itself to the stucco sculptor Johann Baptist Zimmermann and the carver Joachim Dietrich, so who shaped the room depends on which source you read.

findings.before: The Salon de la Princesse in the Hôtel de Soubise in Paris, decorated by Germain Boffrand with paintings by Natoire and others, falls in the 1730s, although sources disagree on the exact years. Britannica says the salons were begun in 1732, Wikipedia gives 1735 to 1740 for Boffrand's interiors, and another source says 1735 to 1739.
findings.after: The Salon de la Princesse in the Hôtel de Soubise in Paris forms part of Germain Boffrand's Rococo interiors, with paintings by Charles Natoire and others. The French National Archives dates the commission for new arrangements to 1732. Boffrand's oval pavilion followed in 1735, with work on the interiors beginning in 1736; the Archives' timeline dates the oval pavilion and interior decoration to 1735 to 1740.
